newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip, rate trend unclear on US data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip, rate trend unclear on US data.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were quoted lower on Friday compared with late Thursday but dealers said trading was thin as the market got no clue on further interest rate trends after the day's U.S. jobless data.
MinFins closely track Brady Bonds and other emerging market debt.
The U.S. Labor Department said 175,000 non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in March, fewer than the 293,000 in February and slightly less than had been expected.

"Nobody has a clear opinion about the figures," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said. "Some of them are favourable for the U.S. interest rate, some are not. The market has no clue about the future of the U.S. interest rates."
Emerging markets are speculating about another 25-basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which would affect U.S. Treasury prices.
Dealers said early trading was otherwise quiet ahead of the figures, with levels going down without real deals, except some short covering.
"Not much happened in early trading as everybody seemed awaiting a push from U.S. data," one dealer said.

Coursault said: "Today's figures are a bit in favour of another rate hike, so the market should not go up... The other problem about Russia now is that no good news is expected from there. We do not trade on Russia, we trade on U.S.Treasuries."
